text.p: - A top nuclear physicist has committed suicide to protest against the disastrous financial state of a leading nuclear research centre, according to one of the versions being considered by police.
- The Moscow administration expects that carmaker "Moskvich" might interest foreign investors once it is declared bankrupt and government control is established.
- Moscow mayor Yuri Lyzhkov wants Sevastopol, which has long been the main navy base of the Russian Black Sea Fleet, to be confirmed as a Russian city.
- While Russia and the United States are accusing each other of being perfidious, the signing of a treaty on regional missile defences has been postponed.
- The Russian government will toughen tax collecting measures, first deputy finance minister Vladimir Petrov says.
- The appointment of Boris Berezovsky to the Security Council has been welcomed in Chechnya despite strong critisism among Russia's politicians.
- Viktor Chernomyrdin, Anatoly Chubais and Boris Yeltsin top the list of 100 leading politicians, according to the paper's survey in october.
- An idea for Russia's participation in the political structures of NATO has been worked out in President Boris Yeltsin's administration, the paper says.

- If the government does not undertake urgent measures to solve financial problems in the army, the situation might get out of control, the paper quotes officials form the military workers' trade union as saying.
- President Yeltsin's operation might take place any day next week. He has been well prepared, says US cardiologist Michael DeBakey.

- Yeltsin's younger daughter, Tatyana Dyachenko, has become the president's main source of information and has initiated some of the latest Kremlin reshuffles, writes the daily, referring to Boris Berezovsky's appointment as deputy security chief.

- Russia is planning to set up a free economic zone in Chechnya with Boris Berezovsky establishing his control over the oil sector, the paper says in reference to the appointment of one of the Russia's most influencial businessmen to have a say in matters on the Security Council concerning the rebel region.
